slam.title: SLAM with Cartographer (run with a Gazebo world)

nav.title: Nav2 with the map shipped in turtlebot3_navigation2 (TurtleBot3 World)
Navigation2 with a saved map (run with a Gazebo world)
nav.cmd: ros2 launch turtlebot3_navigation2 navigation2.launch.py use_sim_time:=True map:=$HOME/map.yaml

real.title: Real TurtleBot3 (run on the robot's Raspberry Pi)
real.needs: a TurtleBot3 with OpenCR board and LDS-01/02/03 lidar
real.notes: Set LDS_MODEL to LDS-01, LDS-02 or LDS-03 to match the lidar, and TURTLEBOT3_MODEL to burger or waffle. Run teleop/SLAM/Nav2 on the remote PC with the same ROS_DOMAIN_ID.

steps: sudo apt install python3-vcstool python3-colcon-common-extensions python3-rosdep

honesty: The site runs these real launch files, YAML, URDF/xacro and SDF files in the browser and models the programs they start (gz sim, controller_manager, move_group, Nav2 servers ...) in JavaScript. It cannot run the compiled C++ nodes. On a real Ubuntu 24.04 + ROS 2 Jazzy machine the same workspace builds and runs with the steps below.
pruned: Only the mesh/texture files used by the robots and worlds listed in 'gallery' and the entries are shipped (vcs import gets the complete repositories).
